tools.desc: The most widely used AI assistant. Answers questions, writes, makes images, searches the web and talks out loud.
tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.start: Sign up free, then ask it to explain something you've always wondered about.

tools.desc: AI assistant known for careful, natural writing and for reading long documents. Strong at coding and analysis.
tools.name: Claude
tools.start: Upload a long PDF and ask for the five most important points.

tools.desc: Google's AI assistant. Works with Gmail, Docs and Maps, makes images and video, and has a live voice mode.
tools.name: Gemini
tools.start: Ask it to plan a day out near you, using Google Maps.

tools.desc: Microsoft's AI assistant, built into Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365 apps like Word, Excel and Outlook.
tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.start: Open Copilot in Windows and ask it to summarize a web page you're reading.

tools.desc: An AI search engine that answers in plain language and shows a numbered source for every claim.
tools.name: Perplexity
tools.start: Ask a question you'd normally search for, then click the sources to check them.

tools.desc: Upload your own notes, PDFs or videos and ask questions about them, or turn them into a podcast-style audio summary. Called NotebookLM until July 2026.
tools.name: Gemini Notebook
tools.start: Upload a document you need to understand and generate an audio overview.

tools.desc: Checks spelling, grammar and tone as you type in email, documents and websites, and can rewrite sentences.
tools.name: Grammarly
tools.start: Install the browser extension and write an email as usual.

tools.desc: AI inside the Notion notes app. Summarizes notes, drafts pages and pulls action items from meeting notes.
tools.name: Notion AI
tools.start: Paste meeting notes into a page and ask for a list of action items.

tools.desc: Records meetings and calls, writes a transcript as people talk, and produces a summary afterwards.
tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.start: Record your next video call and read the summary afterwards.

tools.desc: Creates striking, artistic images from a description. Popular with designers and illustrators.
tools.name: Midjourney
tools.start: Describe a scene with a style and lighting, then try small changes.

tools.desc: Image generator that's especially good at putting readable words into pictures, such as posters and logos.
tools.name: Ideogram
tools.start: Make a birthday card with the person's name written on it.

tools.desc: Adobe's image and video generator, trained on licensed content so it's designed to be safe for commercial use.
tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.start: Generate a product background, then edit it in Photoshop or Adobe Express.

tools.desc: Easy design app with built-in AI that writes text, generates images and resizes designs for you.
tools.name: Canva
tools.start: Pick a social post template and ask the AI to write the caption.

tools.desc: AI video studio: turn text or a photo into short clips, remove backgrounds and edit with AI.
tools.name: Runway
tools.start: Upload a still photo and ask it to animate the scene.

tools.desc: Generates realistic short video clips from a description or an image, with a daily free allowance.
tools.name: Kling
tools.start: Describe a five-second scene, like waves at sunset with birds flying past.

tools.desc: Makes complete songs, with singing and instruments, from a short description or your own lyrics.
tools.name: Suno
tools.start: Ask for an upbeat folk song about your pet.

tools.desc: Turns text into very natural speech in many voices and languages. Used for audiobooks, videos and accessibility.
tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.start: Paste a paragraph and listen to it in three different voices.

tools.desc: A code editor with AI built in. Describe a change in plain English and it edits the code across your project.
tools.name: Cursor
tools.start: Open a small project and ask it to explain what the code does.

tools.bestFor: Developers in VS Code and GitHub
tools.desc: AI coding assistant inside popular code editors. Suggests code as you type and can take on whole tasks.
tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.start: Install it in VS Code and write a comment describing a function you need.

tools.desc: A coding agent that reads your project, plans changes, writes and tests code, and explains what it did.
tools.name: Claude Code
tools.start: Ask it to add a small feature to a project and review its plan first.

models.desc: Not a product but a design, published in the paper "Attention Is All You Need". Almost every modern language model is built on it.
models.name: The Transformer

models.desc: Read text in both directions at once and greatly improved how well computers understood language. It quickly made Google Search better.
models.name: BERT

models.desc: Wrote surprisingly fluent paragraphs. OpenAI first held back the full version over worries about misuse.
models.name: GPT-2

models.desc: 175 billion parameters. The first model that could write, translate, answer questions and code from simple instructions.
models.name: GPT-3

models.desc: Predicted the 3D shape of proteins, a 50-year-old problem in biology. Its creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
models.name: AlphaFold 2

models.desc: Showed that AI could draw pictures from a written description, starting the AI image boom.
models.name: DALL·E

models.desc: Turned plain-English requests into working code and powered the first GitHub Copilot.
models.name: Codex

models.desc: A free, downloadable image generator that anyone could run and adapt, which sparked a huge community of tools.
models.name: Stable Diffusion

models.desc: Reached 100 million users in about two months and made AI chatbots part of everyday life.
models.name: ChatGPT launches

models.desc: Could read images as well as text and scored highly on professional exams like the bar exam.
models.name: GPT-4

models.desc: Built with a strong focus on safety, and among the first to read very long documents in one go.
models.name: Claude and Claude 2

models.desc: A capable language model released for anyone to download and build on, bringing chatbot technology to researchers and small companies.
models.name: Llama 2

models.desc: Google's first model designed from the start to handle text, images, audio and video together.
models.name: Gemini 1.0

models.desc: Introduced the Haiku, Sonnet and Opus sizes. Claude 3.5 Sonnet became a favorite for coding and writing.
models.name: Claude 3 and 3.5

models.desc: Held natural, real-time voice conversations and could see through your camera. The "o" stands for "omni".
models.name: GPT-4o

models.desc: The first widely used reasoning model. It thinks step by step before answering, and is much better at math and logic.
models.name: o1

models.desc: Free-to-download models that came close to the best paid models of the time.
models.name: Llama 3

models.desc: Generated realistic video clips from a text description, a big step for AI video.
models.name: Sora

models.desc: A free, downloadable reasoning model from a Chinese lab that matched top paid models at a fraction of the cost.
models.name: DeepSeek-R1

models.desc: Generated video with matching sound, dialogue and music, all from one description.
models.name: Veo 3

models.desc: Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 could work on coding and agent tasks for hours at a stretch.
models.name: Claude 4

models.desc: Google's first models with built-in thinking, able to read about a million tokens of text at once.
models.name: Gemini 2.5

models.desc: Combined fast answers and deeper reasoning in one system that decides how long to think.
models.name: GPT-5

models.desc: Anthropic's current models: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5, plus Claude Fable 5.2, released November 2026, its most capable model.
models.name: Claude 5 family

models.desc: OpenAI's current generation. In November 2026 it released GPT-6.2 Astra, its most capable model for hard projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a cheaper model for everyday work. ChatGPT's free plan uses GPT-6 Luna.
models.name: GPT-6 family

models.desc: Google's current generation, introduced in October 2026 with Gemini 4 Argon as its frontier model. Carbon, Neon (added November 2026 as a faster, cheaper middle option) and Hydrogen cover everyday tasks across Gemini and Google's products.
models.name: Gemini 4 family
